subject: 📊 Daily Portfolio: Markets closed | 🚨 SPXC exit 33 days overdue, price feed blocked 18th day
html_body:
🚨 URGENT — SPXC

Exit decision (halal defense-rule breach, logged 2026-08-25) is now 33 calendar days / ~24 trading days overdue. Price feed has been fully blocked for the 18th consecutive day (Yahoo query1/query2 + stooq all return EGRESS_BLOCKED), so this cannot be confirmed automatically — but triangulated web snapshots (GuruFocus, Cerbat Gem, multiple sources) consistently put SPXC at $172.55–$174.65 since Sept 22, a fresh 52-week low, well below the $186.90 stop trigger.

Action needed today: Check IBKR directly. If the stop already filled near $186.90, this is closed and portfolio.json just needs reconciling (~-$8.51 net, -8.4%). If it's still open and resting on the bracket while price fell to the $172-175 area, you're carrying a much larger unrealized loss (~-$14 to -$27 net) than the stop was designed to cap — cancel the bracket and exit at market/aggressive marketable limit immediately regardless of price. This is not a "wait and see" situation.

⚠️ WATCH — GOOG

Same price-feed blockage applies here. Unverified snapshot: Sept 25 close $341.08 (+0.61%), Sept 26 intraday range $337.91–$343.60. That's ~2.1% above the $333.90 stop — just outside the formal 2% WATCH band, but Friday (Sept 25) saw a -3.6 to -3.8% one-day drop on Alphabet's capex guide raise ($195-205B, up from $180-190B) plus antitrust/Meta-competition overhang before partially recovering. Not confirmed via a live quote. No action required unless it breaks back down toward the stop — flagging so it's on your radar, not because it's fired.

Market cap is still running well over 2x US GDP — historically every reading this high has preceded a multi-year drawdown. But the aggregate forward P/E (~19.2x) doesn't look nearly as stretched as the cap/GDP ratio implies — that gap is mostly the mega-cap concentration effect (a handful of names, GOOG included, carry an outsized share of total market cap on heavy AI capex).

Implication: keep stops honest and don't lean on "the market will bail me out" — see SPXC above for exactly what happens when a stop isn't confirmed working.

Sources conflicted this run (234.4%-299.5% across providers) — used the multi-source cluster (234-238%), consistent with June's known 232.5% baseline. Verify at currentmarketvaluation.com if precision matters.

📰 Position News — Sept 27, 2026

🟢 GOOG — Federal judge rejected DOJ's push to force a Google ad-exchange sale (early Sept), a meaningful antitrust win. Offset by the FY26 capex guide raise to $195-205B (from $180-190B) driving the Sept 25 -3.6/-3.8% drop; partially recovered by Sept 25 close. Analyst PTs mixed/lower-revised on capex/margin concerns: consensus tracking ~$413-430, Tigress raised to $485 (Sep 22).

🔴 SPXC — Completed the $410M FIS Water bolt-on acquisition Sept 15 (~$105M 2026 revenue, water-management for cooling systems — doesn't touch the Kranze defense segment, doesn't change the exit call). Strong Q2 print (EPS $2.02 beat vs $1.85 est, revenue $679M beat) and a Wolfe Research Outperform initiation haven't stopped the slide to a fresh 52-week low; a sector-wide selloff in air-cooling names (Trane, Modine, Johnson Controls, Carrier) after Nvidia's warm-water-cooling comments added further pressure. Consensus analyst rating is still "Buy"/"Strong Buy" (avg PT $195-272) — irrelevant here since the exit is a halal-compliance call, not a valuation call.

No discovery candidate generated here — that's stock-finder's job, on demand.

🔄 Rotation suggestions

📚 Today you learned

Mean Reversion vs. Value Trap

SPXC just beat Q2 estimates (EPS $2.02 vs $1.85, revenue +23%), got a Wolfe Research Outperform initiation, and still cratered to a fresh 52-week low ~$173, with GuruFocus's own fair-value model pegging it near $194 and consensus analyst targets clustered $195-272 — on paper, "cheap." The trap: none of that matters here, because you're exiting on the halal defense-rule breach, not a valuation call. Mean reversion says "beaten-down + good fundamentals = bounce coming." A value trap says "the market knows something your model doesn't." When your reason for selling is a compliance rule instead of a price target, the stock's cheapness is irrelevant — you don't buy back a name your own halal screen excluded just because the chart looks tempting. Compare GOOG: -3.6% on a real, priced-in reason (capex guide raise) is a normal repricing, not a trap either way — you just watch the stop.

Also today: GF Value — GuruFocus's proprietary fair-value estimate (historical multiples + growth + profitability); useful as one data point, never a reason to override a compliance-driven exit.
